Import an external taxonomic table as a data frame

Source: R/import_taxonomic_table.R
import_taxonomic_table.Rd

Read a taxonomic table from a file (e.g., a .csv file, or an Excel sheet), check its format, and return it as a data frame ready-to-be-used as input of phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy().

It is the mirror of phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() for taxonomic tables. Two tables are used to build a missing_taxa_list from taxonomy: the taxonomy of the tips of the backbone phylogeny (type = "backbone"), and the description of the taxa to graft (type = "missing_taxa"). Each one is read with a call of the function.

Taxonomic tables are the go-to option for large phylogenies with neatly defined taxonomic levels (see Details).

Usage

import_taxonomic_table(
  file,
  type,
  phy = NULL,
  sep = NULL,
  sheet = 1,
  reader = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

file

Character string. Path to the file with the table. The format is chosen from the extension of the file: ".csv" (comma-separated), ".tsv", ".tab" or ".txt" (tab-separated), ".xlsx" or ".xls" (Excel, requires the package readxl). Use sep or reader for other formats. All the columns are read as text. Blank cells and NA are missing values.

type

Character string. The type of table to read:

  • "backbone" for the taxonomy of the tips of the backbone phylogeny (one row per tip),

  • "missing_taxa" for the description of the taxa to graft (one row per taxon). See Details for the columns of each one.

phy

An object of class "phylo", or NULL. Optional backbone phylogeny, used to check the table against its tips: all the tips of a "backbone" table must be tips of phy, and no taxon of a "missing_taxa" table can already be a tip of phy. Default is NULL, with no check against the phylogeny (it is anyway done by phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy()).

sep

Character string. Field separator of a text file. Default is NULL, to choose it from the extension of the file: "," for .csv, and a tab for .tsv, .tab and .txt. Semicolons are also used inside the cells of the table of the missing taxa (to separate the excluded subclades, and their stems), so do not use them as field separator, and quote the cells that contain commas (e.g., allowed_states).

sheet

Character string or integer. Only used for Excel files. Name or position of the sheet to read. Default is 1. Both taxonomic tables can be stored in two sheets of the same Excel file, and read with two calls.

reader

Function. Optional function used to read file, to import any other format (e.g., .ods, or an export of an online spreadsheet). It must take the path of the file as first argument and return a data frame. If provided, it is used whatever the extension of the file. Default is NULL.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print a summary of the table. Default is TRUE.

...

Further arguments passed to the function reading the file (utils::read.table() for text files, readxl::read_excel() for Excel files, or reader).

Value

A data frame with only character columns, ready to be used as backbone_taxonomic_table (if type = "backbone") or missing_taxa_taxonomic_table (if type = "missing_taxa") in phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy(). Blank cells are NA.

Details

When to use taxonomic tables

Taxonomic tables are the go-to option for large phylogenies with neatly defined taxonomic levels (e.g., Family, Subfamily, Tribe, Genus). The taxonomy of the backbone is provided once, and each taxon to graft only needs its own taxonomic levels: the constraints (target clade, sister clade, excluded subclades) are written with the names of the groups or of the taxonomic levels to use, and the clades are retrieved from the phylogeny. The same group is therefore always the same clade, whatever the number of taxa, which avoids the typos and inconsistencies of clades written taxon by taxon, and the tables can be taken as such from a taxonomic database.

The limit is that only the taxonomic groups of the backbone table can be used as clades. To fine-tune the grafting of some taxa with any other node of the phylogeny (e.g., a clade without a name, a part of a group, or a group of several genera), define their clades by tips or node IDs with phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list() or phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() (see 'Fine-tuning the clades' in their Details sections).

Both routes return the same missing_taxa_list, so a list built from taxonomic tables can be adjusted afterwards.

Backbone table (type = "backbone")

One row per tip of the backbone phylogeny. The column Taxa (Required) holds the tip labels, and must have unique values. All the other columns are taxonomic levels (e.g., Family, Subfamily, Tribe, Genus, but they can be anything), usually from the broadest to the narrowest. At least one level is required. The values of a level are the names of the taxonomic groups (e.g., "Homo" for a "Genus"). Levels do not have to be informed for all the tips: blank cells and NA are missing values.

Missing taxa table (type = "missing_taxa")

One row per taxon to graft. The columns Taxa (Required; unique names of the taxa to graft) and Type (Required; "taxa" or "clades") are required. The next columns are the taxonomic levels of the taxa to graft, with the same names as in the backbone table, and the addtional constraints:

  • Target_clade (Required for Type = "taxa") or Sister_clade (Required for Type = "clades"): A single taxonomic group, written either as the name of the group (e.g., "Homo"), or as the name of a taxonomic level (e.g., "Genus"). If a taxonomic level is provided, the group will be identified as recorded in the column of the same name in missing_taxa_taxonomic_table (e.g., "Genus" with Genus = "Camponotus" gives the clade of the genus Camponotus). It is an error if the group is absent from the backbone, or if the taxon has no value at the requested level.

  • Excluded_subclades (Optional, Type = "taxa"): Subclades of the target clade where the taxon is known not to belong, separated by semicolons (e.g., "Pheidole; Camponotus"). Each one is a group or a level name, as in Target_clade.

  • $include_target_clade_stem (Optional, Type = "taxa"): Logical. Whether the stem branch of the target clade is a valid placement to graft this taxa (NA or empty cell uses the global argument set in the grafting function).

  • $exclude_subclades_stem (Optional, Type = "taxa"): Logical. Whether the stem branch of the excluded clade(s) is/are a excluded from grafting too. Separated by semicolons if multiple Excluded_subclades are provided (NA or empty cell uses the global argument set in the grafting function).

  • $allowed_states (Optional): For each taxon, the states of a simmap in which it can be grafted (see the simmap argument of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() or phylograftR::graft_missing_clades()), separated by commas. If multiple traits are used, each set of states must be separated by semicolons (e.g., "blue, red; low"). It is accepted with both Target_clade and Sister_clade. (NA or empty cell uses the global argument set in the grafting function).

Checks

The function checks that the required columns are present, that names of columns are unique, that Taxa is never empty and always unique, and, for the table of the missing taxa, that Type is valid. Names of columns and values are stripped from the spaces around them. Rows with only blank cells (e.g., the trailing rows of a spreadsheet) are dropped.

The other checks (e.g., names of levels and groups, consistency with the backbone, and the groups used as clades) are done when the clades are retrieved, by phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy().

See also

Other functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() to read a table of missing taxa from a file, with clades defined by tips or node IDs (for fine-tuning).

  • phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy() to build the missing_taxa_list from the taxonomic tables.

Author

Maël Doré

Examples

# Paths to example tables, provided with the package
backbone_path <- system.file("extdata", "toy_backbone_taxonomic_table.csv", package = "phylograftR")
missing_taxa_path <- system.file("extdata", "toy_missing_taxa_taxonomic_table.csv",
                                 package = "phylograftR")

# Load the associated backbone phylogeny
data(toy_backbone)

# Import the taxonomy of the backbone: one row per tip, one column per taxonomic level
backbone_taxonomic_table <- import_taxonomic_table(file = backbone_path, type = "backbone",
                                                   phy = toy_backbone)
#> Backbone taxonomic table: 30 tips, with 4 taxonomic level(s): Family, Subfamily, Tribe, Genus
head(backbone_taxonomic_table)
#>   Taxa   Family Subfamily     Tribe Genus
#> 1  t26 Family_A Subfam_A2 Tribe_A2a  <NA>
#> 2   t2 Family_A Subfam_A2 Tribe_A2a  <NA>
#> 3  t21 Family_A Subfam_A2 Tribe_A2a  <NA>
#> 4  t16 Family_A Subfam_A2 Tribe_A2a  <NA>
#> 5  t11 Family_A Subfam_A2 Tribe_A2a  <NA>
#> 6   t4 Family_A Subfam_A2 Tribe_A2a  <NA>

# Import the description of the taxa to graft: one row per taxon
missing_taxa_taxonomic_table <- import_taxonomic_table(file = missing_taxa_path,
                                                       type = "missing_taxa",
                                                       phy = toy_backbone)
#> Missing taxa taxonomic table: 10 taxa to graft (7 as 'taxa', 3 as 'clades'), with 9 other column(s): Family, Subfamily, Tribe, Genus, Target_clade, Sister_clade, Excluded_subclades, include_target_clade_stem, exclude_subclades_stem
missing_taxa_taxonomic_table
#>           Taxa   Type   Family Subfamily     Tribe   Genus Target_clade
#> 1      New_sp1   taxa Family_A      <NA>      <NA>    <NA>       Family
#> 2      New_sp2   taxa Family_A      <NA>      <NA>    <NA>       Family
#> 3      New_sp3   taxa Family_A      <NA>      <NA>    <NA>       Family
#> 4      New_sp4   taxa Family_B      <NA>      <NA>    <NA>     Family_B
#> 5      New_sp5   taxa Family_B Subfam_B1      <NA>    <NA>    Subfamily
#> 6      New_sp6   taxa Family_B Subfam_B2  Tribe_B2    <NA>        Gen_2
#> 7      New_sp7   taxa Family_B Subfam_B2  Tribe_B2    <NA>        Tribe
#> 8  Genus_a_sp1 clades Family_B Subfam_B1      <NA> Genus_a         <NA>
#> 9  Genus_a_sp2 clades Family_B Subfam_B1      <NA> Genus_a         <NA>
#> 10 Genus_b_sp1 clades Family_A Subfam_A1 Tribe_A1b Genus_b         <NA>
#>    Sister_clade  Excluded_subclades include_target_clade_stem
#> 1          <NA> Subfam_A1;Tribe_A2a                      TRUE
#> 2          <NA>     Tribe_A2a;Gen_3                      TRUE
#> 3          <NA>                <NA>                     FALSE
#> 4          <NA>                <NA>                      <NA>
#> 5          <NA>               Gen_1                      TRUE
#> 6          <NA>                <NA>                      <NA>
#> 7          <NA>                <NA>                     FALSE
#> 8         Gen_1                <NA>                      <NA>
#> 9         Gen_1                <NA>                      <NA>
#> 10        Tribe                <NA>                      <NA>
#>    exclude_subclades_stem
#> 1              TRUE;FALSE
#> 2              FALSE;TRUE
#> 3                    <NA>
#> 4                    <NA>
#> 5                    <NA>
#> 6                    <NA>
#> 7                    <NA>
#> 8                    <NA>
#> 9                    <NA>
#> 10                   <NA>

# The tables are the datasets provided with the package
data(toy_backbone_taxonomic_table)
data(toy_missing_taxa_taxonomic_table)
identical(backbone_taxonomic_table, toy_backbone_taxonomic_table)
#> [1] TRUE
# (the logical column include_target_clade_stem of the dataset is read as text from the file)
all(mapply(function (x, y) identical(as.character(x), y),
           toy_missing_taxa_taxonomic_table, missing_taxa_taxonomic_table))
#> [1] TRUE

# Use them to build the lists of missing taxa
missing_taxa_lists <- build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy(
  backbone_taxonomic_table = backbone_taxonomic_table,
  missing_taxa_taxonomic_table = missing_taxa_taxonomic_table,
  phy = toy_backbone, verbose = FALSE)
names(missing_taxa_lists)
#> [1] "taxa"   "clades"

# Use them to graft the taxa
grafted_phy <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = toy_backbone, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_lists$taxa,
                                  verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)
